Nope, butr they did get a bleed card (sort of).

Fiendish Tounge:
Requires a Sabbat Vampire
(D) Bleed at +1 bleed. Anarch vampires get -1 intercept when
attempting to block this action. If this acting vampire is a Tzimsce
(symbol) and the bleed is successful (for 1 or more), this vampire may
burn 1 blood to untap during your discard phase this turn.

It's not crazy strong, but it's good enough to eclipse Computer
Hacking in most Sabbat decks.

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <f987c6cd.03052...@posting.google.com>, vermillian

<vermil...@yahoo.com> writes:
>Questions like "What if Ventrue had won the thing? Would they have
>made it Camerilla only + bleeder, or did they have something prepared
>for each clan specifically, or was this card made after they won?" all
>should be raised... just to see if playtesting happens or not.

Given that it was a tournament in the fall, it seems more than plausible
that a special ability could be worked out afterwards. Or - once the
results were looking fairly firm - several groups given different cards
to playtest. Or have five cards, each of which was looking to get
something added to it for a winning clan (something votey, something
bleedy, something rushy etc.)

When you know you're handing control to the players, it would be very
odd for the designers to not think up several contingency plans in
advance - the obvious problematic one being, "What if a bloodline wins?"

--
